## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
10 + 20
```

```{r}
5*5
```

#Dataset description: This dataset includes sixteen columns and 50000 rows. Each row represents an individual student, shown by their student ID number. The columns include information describing student interactions with AI, spanning academic outcomes, behavioral patterns, institutional context, and psychological well-being. Students are categorized by their major, year of study, pre and post-semester GPA, hours studying with and without use of AI, whether or not they have a paid subscription, their percieved dependency on AI, anxiety level during exams, and burnout risk. 

# Data manipulation/cleaning

## Question 1: Each winning ticket consists of 5 randomly drawn numbers and one powerball number (the last number on the ticket), create a new column for each one of these numbers separately (num1, num2, num3, num4, num5, powerball).

```{r}
# Code for question 1
lottery_clean <- Lottery_data |> 
  mutate(numbers_list = str_extract_all(Winning.Numbers, "\\d+")) |> 
  mutate(num1 = as.numeric(map_chr(numbers_list, 1)),
         num2 = as.numeric(map_chr(numbers_list, 2)),
         num3 = as.numeric(map_chr(numbers_list, 3)),
         num4 = as.numeric(map_chr(numbers_list, 4)),
         num5 = as.numeric(map_chr(numbers_list, 5)),
         powerball = as.numeric(map_chr(numbers_list, 6))) |> 
  select(-numbers_list)
         
```
